subject: Follow-up: continuous batch patterns & budget alignment for NovaHealth
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Connor Briggs <connor@novahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: quick clarifications on batching / concurrency assumptions

Connor — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick follow-up to lock in the two inputs we need to produce a scoped cost estimate and Hosted vs Dedicated recommendation. TL;DR: if you can confirm the three bullets below we’ll turn around a 2‑page cost bake with per-1M-token unit numbers and expected p95 token latency given continuous batching.

Key asks (one-line answers welcome):
- Traffic shape: what’s your expected average tokens/day and expected 95th percentile of tokens/minute for peak hours? (we saw the 200 req/s ballpark in the call — if that was peak, say so)
- Live vs async split: what fraction of requests are streaming/low-latency (user-facing chat) vs background/async (batch scoring, embeddings)?
- Latency SLO for live requests: target p95 for token-delivery or for full-response? (examples: p95 token latency <200ms and full-response <1.2s)

Notes on how we’ll use these: Redwood’s continuous batching pools prefer a steady inflight window (e.g., 50–200ms batch window) to maximize batching gains while meeting low-latency SLOs. If you have many short streaming sessions (~1–3 replies each) we’ll surface those as small windows and rely on prefix caching to reduce compute. If loads are bursty (daily sync jobs, long tail spikes) we’ll call those out and show how Dedicated reserved capacity vs hosted on-demand pricing changes unit $/1M tokens.

I’ve attached a tiny traffic sample template you can drop numbers into — if you reply with that we’ll include a sensitivity table (±25% volume) and a target $/1M-token band for procurement.

Next steps:
- You reply with the three bullets and (optionally) the attached CSV sample filled in.
- We’ll return an ops-aligned estimate and recommended configuration (batch windows, target concurrency, cache settings) by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
[attachment: nova_traffic_samples.csv (csv)]

From: Connor Briggs <connor@novahealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@novahealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 18:47:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick clarifications on batching / concurrency assumptions

Thanks Olga — quick answers inline.

- Traffic shape: avg ~45M tokens/day right now; planning to ramp to ~200M tokens/day over next 6–9 months. Peak minute observed during morning syncs is ~1.6M tokens/minute (~26.6k tokens/sec) but that’s aggregated across internal batch jobs and user traffic. The user-facing side is closer to 300–600 tokens/sec during peak minutes.
- Live vs async split: roughly 60% live (chat/web UI) and 40% async (batch scoring and nightly enrichment). Live requests are mostly streaming; async are large multi-k requests.
- Latency SLO: for live we want p95 full-response <800ms; token streaming p95 ideally <150ms. Full-response for async can be minutes — not constrained.

Notes: we attached a quick sample of recent traffic by hour (nova_traffic_samples.csv). For budgeting the procurement team asked for target unit economics between $80–$130 per 1M tokens as an acceptable range — lower is great but procurement will review. They also asked for a Hosted vs Dedicated comparison showing where reserved capacity starts to make sense.

Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up Tuesday if helpful.

Connor
Director, ML Platform | NovaHealth
connor@novahealth.com
[attachment: nova_traffic_samples.csv (csv)]

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Connor Briggs <connor@novahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick clarifications on batching / concurrency assumptions

Connor — perfect, thanks for the details and the CSV. I skimmed the sample and a couple of quick observations before we run the formal estimate:

- Mixed workload: the large async multi-k requests (nightly enrichment) will benefit from longer batch aggregation windows and quantized model picks (we’ll show a cached-quantized variant for scoring jobs). That alone can drop unit cost by ~25% vs non-quantized hosted on-demand assumptions.
- Live streaming: given your p95 targets (<800ms full-response, <150ms token) we’ll recommend a continuous batching window of 40–80ms for user-facing pools to get batching benefits without violating the SLO. This assumes median tokens-per-request ~400; if your user requests trend much shorter (50–100 tokens) we’ll widen concurrency to keep aggregation effective.
- Cache expectations: if prefix cache hit rate is 10–20% we’ll include that uplift in the sensitivity table; if it’s >40% we’ll show a best-case band. Please indicate any known reuse (templates, repeated prompts).

Preliminary cost guidance (high-level rough numbers for discussion only):
- Hosted (on-demand): expect ~$160–$210 per 1M tokens at your peak mix (streaming + async) with default non-quantized models.
- Hosted with quantized scoring variant for async: ~$120–$165 per 1M tokens (depends on async fraction and batch window tuning).
- Dedicated (reserved pool, 1yr commit): $70–$110 per 1M tokens assuming stable 200M tokens/day and proper autoscale/burst config.

Action items I’ll run before our next touch:
1) Produce a 2‑page cost bake for Hosted vs Dedicated + sensitivity table (±25% volume, ±10% cache hit).
2) Add an appendix showing recommended batch windows, per-pool concurrency, and estimated p95 token latency numbers for the chosen model family.
3) Include a short note on how prefix/KV cache and continuous batching interplay for streaming sessions (help procurement understand the unit economics drivers).

Can you confirm whether you have a steady pool of templated prompts (yes/no) and whether you can share a small set of representative sessions (anonymized) for latency profiling?

If yes, Ben and I will assemble the estimate and loop in Marissa for Dedicated pricing options and contractual terms. Otherwise we’ll run with assumed template reuse at 15%.

Thanks — will aim to send the bake by EOD today (Pacific).

— Olga
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[attachment: nova_estimate_workbook.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Connor Briggs <connor@novahealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick clarifications on batching / concurrency assumptions

Thanks — confirmed.
- Templates: yes, we have ~120 canonical templates that cover ~70% of live traffic. I’ll drop a small anonymized sample of 25 sessions into the Drive link below by EOD.
- Drive sample: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1sampleAnonSessions

Procurement will want the Dedicated cost breakout (1yr vs 3yr) and a clear migration plan from Hosted to Dedicated (we expect ramp risk in months 1–3). Also include an estimate of the expected slot warm-up/scale latency (how long until Dedicated autoscale brings additional GPUs online under sustained spikes).

We’re good for a Tuesday 10:00am ET touch to review the bake. Please send calendar invite.

Connor
Director, ML Platform | NovaHealth
